title: Downed power lines
scenario: Power line down on the street, sparking wire on the ground or on a car after the earthquake.
steps: Stay at least 35 feet away — about the length of a bus. Assume every downed line is live, even if it looks dead.
Never touch a person or object in contact with the line; electricity can travel through them into you.
If a line falls on your car while you are inside: stay in the car and call 911. Wait for rescuers.
Only if the car is on fire and you must get out: jump clear so you never touch the car and the ground at the same time, land with feet together, and shuffle away with small steps.
Water conducts electricity — keep far from puddles touching any wire.
do_not: Do not drive over downed lines.
Do not try to move a line with a stick, rope, or any object.
